object_description: three linked gabled volumes arranged along the slope
design_condition: The volumes follow the slope-facing scale of the neighboring residential area along the development boundary, linking the complex into a whole while assigning uses along the street according to their public character.

positive.statement: The precise analysis of the location provides the basis for a promising urban-planning strategy.

position.rationale: Urban-planning assessment applies broadly to the linear site arrangement along the slope.

positive.statement: The row of houses takes up the scale of the adjacent residential area and respects the development boundary.

position.rationale: Three linked gabled volumes visibly form a settlement-scaled row along the development boundary.

positive.statement: All buildings are reached calmly from the street via landscape paths.

position.rationale: Approach paths are estimated along the open spaces between and around the linked volumes.

positive.statement: Addressing the clinic independently is correct.

position.rationale: The independently addressed clinic is approximated at the eastern end of the linear composition.

positive.statement: Dividing the uses into three buildings creates ecologically interesting landscape permeability.

position.rationale: Permeability judgment is distributed through the open gaps separating the three volumes.

negative.statement: The inclusion of the old villa strains the overall concept, while the school addition strongly confuses the existing building.

position.rationale: Existing-building conflict is approximated at the western end of the linked composition.

negative.statement: The urban-planning approach is promising, but its implementation cannot be achieved volumetrically.

position.rationale: Volumetric implementation concern applies across the full three-volume arrangement.

negative.statement: The actual entrances are not clearly visible from the bus stop and are not accessible for disabled users.

position.rationale: Entrances are approximated along the street-facing lower edge of the composition.

negative.statement: The differentiation of ramps and stairs leads to unnecessary complexity.

position.rationale: Circulation complexity is estimated within the site approaches between linked volumes.

negative.statement: The clinic entrances are lightless corridors and do not have the desired spatial qualities.

position.rationale: Clinic entry corridors are approximated within the eastern volume.

negative.statement: Dividing the intensive care unit over two floors is not operationally conceivable, and direct access from the wards is missing.

position.rationale: The unit is not distinguishable; its multi-level concern is anchored within the upper eastern mass.

negative.statement: The desired separation of adult and children's entrances and cloakrooms in the gym is missing.

position.target: adult and children's entrances and cloakrooms
position.rationale: Gym entry separation is approximated near the public-facing approach edge.

negative.statement: The underground car-park arrangement creates a complex and long tunnel access route.

position.rationale: Tunnel access is assigned beneath the street-facing site edge, absent from the exterior sample.

negative.statement: The station outdoor spaces appear closed off and lack a more direct connection to the landscape.

position.rationale: Outdoor-space enclosure is approximated along the southern landscape edge of the linked development.
